cards.title: Statistical Analysis of Resistance Trends
cards.claim: Trends in CFR over time were assessed using the Cochran-Armitage test for trend. Confidence intervals for CFR were calculated using the Newcombe-Wilson method without continuity correction. Statistical significance (p < 0.05) indicates a trend in the ability to achieve PD targets, but clinical significance must be evaluated separately.
conditions: Applied to CFR values grouped into time intervals (e.g., 3-year periods).
Used to determine if changes in MIC distributions significantly impacted predicted efficacy.
required_inputs: CFR values for each time interval.
Sample sizes/isolate counts for each interval (implicit in the test).
limitations: Statistical significance does not guarantee clinical relevance (e.g., small CFR declines may be statistically significant but clinically negligible).
Depends on the accuracy of the underlying MIC surveillance data.
Does not adjust for multiple comparisons across multiple regimens in the description.
cards.downstream_use: Provides a quantitative measure of whether resistance trends are strong enough to alter the predicted efficacy of a drug regimen over time.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
